statusText: NQ futures have entered the CME Friday-evening weekend halt (5:00pm ET / market week close), roughly 2.5 hours after the U.S. cash close, leaving no live price path to evaluate. Since the prior run (21:29 UTC), no new developments have emerged: the Strait of Hormuz crisis remains at its previously confirmed state -- the Thursday-evening two-tanker ADNOC drone attack plus a separate drone strike on an exiting tanker remain the latest confirmed incidents, with Qatar/Kuwait/Egypt/Bahrain condemnations already priced in as ongoing background risk and no new discrete escalation identified. VIX closed the Friday session calm at 14.63 (+0.55%), confirming the low-volatility close already observed last hour. The 10-year Treasury yield holds near 4.696% (+5bp), still attributed to Friday's soft Retail Sales print plus the standing (non-escalatory) U.S. rhetoric that its naval blockade of Iranian ports could continue "indefinitely"; WTI holds in the flat mid-$81 area with no new driver identified. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota remains exhausted this run (two calls, both rate_limit errors), so this run again relies entirely on WebSearch corroboration of already-known facts; Confidence is further reduced this hour because NQ itself is now in the weekend halt and there is no live price structure to assess.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Tail falls to 2% (low) as NQ enters the CME weekend halt with no live price-path evidence available to assess for failed-pullback or repeated-extension structure. Stress falls to 12% (low) as the cash session's already-digested drivers (UMich sentiment miss, Retail Sales miss, Broadcom/Applied Materials weakness offset by AMD's resolved-higher move) stop actively repricing; the standing Strait of Hormuz crisis remains a contained background driver rather than an actively repricing one. Confidence eases to 37% (low) reflecting the continued Alpha Vantage outage and the absence of any live NQ price action to evaluate during the halt, offset by clean corroboration that nothing material changed since the prior run. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active regardless of the current EA_ON state. The next evidence-relevant checkpoint is CME's Sunday reopen (~22:00-23:00 UTC / 00:00-01:00 CEST Monday), where any weekend Hormuz headline could produce a gap; a Tail upgrade would require an observed failed-pullback/repeated-extension reaction in NQ itself at or after that reopen, not the standing headline risk alone.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (6-16%) through the trailing 24 hours, easing from Thursday evening's post-CPI/PPI digestion through Friday's Asian/European session into a stable single-digit floor, holding 7-9% through today's confirmed UMich/Retail Sales misses and the Broadcom/Applied Materials semis drag, easing further to 6% as AMD's prior ambiguity resolved higher into the Friday close, and finally to 2% this hour as NQ enters the CME weekend halt with no live price-path evidence to evaluate. Stress ran from the upper-30s Thursday evening down to a low of 23% in the early Friday Asian session, rebuilt through the European morning and the confirmed UMich print (peaking near 44%), held roughly 40-41% through the U.S. afternoon, eased to 34% as the cash session ended, and fell further to 12% this hour as the weekend halt began and today's semis-earnings dispersion stopped actively repricing. The standing Strait of Hormuz crisis provided a persistent, contained event-importance driver throughout. No published assessment exists for the 20:00 UTC hour (a run did not publish in that window).
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to hold at the low weekend floor (~2%) through the entire 24-hour horizon as NQ futures remain in the CME weekend halt with no live session to evaluate; the horizon ends at 21:00 UTC Sunday, one hour before CME's scheduled Sunday reopen (~22:00 UTC), which sits just beyond this window. Stress is projected to decay quickly from 12% this hour to a low weekend floor (~7%) held there by the absence of any active session rather than a resolved risk picture -- the standing Strait of Hormuz crisis remains the principal source of weekend headline/gap risk into Sunday's reopen. No forecast slot currently implies an action change from EA_ON. Confidence is projected to decay gradually from the high-30s toward the mid-20s as the horizon moves further from this run's live evidence and further from any live trading session.
